mainTopic: Gifts that name a valid receiver together with another party: "you and a donkey", and "to you and your sons"
overview: The amud opens with רבי אבין explaining רבי אבהו's ruling. A father who compares his son's acquiring to that of his unborn children is like someone who says "acquire like a donkey", so the son gets nothing. The גמרא then brings a three-way מחלוקת about "you and a donkey": רב נחמן says the person gets half, רב המנונא says the statement means nothing, and רב ששת says the person gets everything. רב ששת tries to prove his view from separating תרומה from a cucumber. The גמרא rejects the proof using רבי אילעא's teaching that even poor produce is real תרומה by Torah law. Next, רב אויא challenges רב המנונא from a משנה about a man who betrothed five women, two of them sisters, and רב אשי answers that challenge. A new case follows: a man gives his property "to you and your sons", and רב יוסף rules that the wife gets half, based on "for אהרן and his sons". אביי pushes back, and the גמרא brings real cases decided by שמואל, רבי יוחנן and רבי, then sets aside the tax case. The amud ends with רבי זירא challenging רב יוסף from a מנחה brought in two vessels, sixty in one vessel and forty in the other.

steps.title: Explaining רבי אבהו's reasoning: "Acquire like a donkey"
steps.stepSummary: After the explanation was approved in the בית מדרש, רבי ירמיה goes to רבי אבין. רבי אבין explains that comparing the son to the unborn children is like saying "acquire like a donkey", which gives the son nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He nodded his head in approval of this in the study hall. He went to him, and he said to him: If someone said to another person "Acquire like a donkey does", would he acquire anything?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story from the previous section. רבי אבין then explains the logic of רבי אבהו's ruling with a comparison to a donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey cannot own property at all. So if the giver says "acquire the way a donkey acquires", he has really given nothing. In the same way, the father tied his son's acquiring to his unborn children, who cannot acquire yet. So the son gets nothing either.

keyTerms.meaning: "Acquire like a donkey": an acquisition compared to one that cannot happen
Does he acquire? (a question that expects the answer: no)

steps.confusionAlert: "Acquire like a donkey" does not mean the person turns into a donkey. It means his acquiring is compared to a donkey's, and a donkey cannot acquire anything.

phrases.english: And he nodded his head at it in the study hall.
He went to him, and he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה went to רבי אבין, and רבי אבין is the one who speaks.

phrases.english: If he had said to him: "Acquire like a donkey,"
would he acquire?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ אֲמַר לֵיהּ קְנִי כַּחֲמוֹר מִי קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about רבי אבהו's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי אבהו rule that the son acquires nothing?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Linking the son to unborn children is like saying "acquire like a donkey", and that gives nothing.

steps.title: Source: "Acquire like a donkey" gives nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רבי אבין's comparison with an accepted teaching: "acquire like a donkey" does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: "Acquire like a donkey" — he does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known ruling to show that the donkey comparison really does mean the person gets nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling is not disputed. Since a donkey cannot acquire, an acquisition modeled on a donkey's is empty. This gives רבי אבין's explanation a firm base.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (introduces a teaching of the אמוראים)

phrases.english: As it was stated:
"Acquire like a donkey" — he does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the comparison used in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That comparing an acquisition to a donkey's makes it empty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted ruling that "קני כחמור" does not acquire.

steps.title: The three-way dispute about "You and a donkey"
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the giver says "you and a donkey" should acquire. רב נחמן says the person gets half. רב המנונא says the statement means nothing. רב ששת says the person gets everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You and a donkey": רב נחמן says he acquires half. רב המנונא says he has said nothing. רב ששת says he acquires all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The same teaching goes on to a harder case, where a person and a donkey are named together. Three אמוראים disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן splits the gift in two, so the person keeps his half. רב המנונא says that tying the person to the donkey ruins the whole gift. רב ששת says the giver knew a donkey cannot acquire, so he really meant everything to go to the person.

keyTerms.meaning: "You and a donkey": a person named together with something that cannot acquire
He said nothing; the statement has no effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In "acquire like a donkey" everyone agrees the person gets nothing. The dispute is only about "you and a donkey".
steps.whyThisMatters: These three positions give the basic choices for any gift that names a valid receiver together with an invalid one.

phrases.english: "You and a donkey" —
Rav Naḥman says: He acquires half,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: and Rav Hamnuna says: He has said nothing.
And Rav Sheshet says: He acquires all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ וַחֲמוֹר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר קָנָה מֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same quoted teaching with a second case that is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "You and a donkey": רב נחמן says half, רב המנונא says nothing, רב ששת says all.

steps.title: רב ששת brings the cucumber ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes רבי יוסי. Only the inside of a cucumber can be bitter. So a person separating תרומה adds more than just the outer part and separates it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From where do I say this? As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says, the only part of a cucumber that is bitter is its inside. Therefore, when a person separates תרומה, he adds to its outer part and separates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins to prove his view that the person acquires everything. In this step he only lays out the source; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bitter inside of a cucumber is not fit to be תרומה, while the outside is. The ברייתא says the person adds more cucumber and separates it all. This means the תרומה includes both a fit part and an unfit part.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
As it is taught in a ברייתא
The inner part / the outer part

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say this?
As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ מַר בַּקִּישּׁוּת, אֶלָּא פְּנִימִי שֶׁבּוֹ.
phrases.english: Nothing in the cucumber is bitter except its inner part.
Therefore, when he separates teruma —
he adds to its outer part, and separates teruma.
phrases.notes: He adds extra cucumber so there is enough good, edible תרומה, and then separates all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת starts the proof for his opinion from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that "you and a donkey" acquires everything.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ברייתא about separating תרומה from a cucumber.

steps.title: The proof: the cucumber is a case of "You and a donkey"
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks why the תרומה works at all, since it mixes a fit part with an unfit part. This shows that something invalid joined to something valid does not cancel the valid part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it work? It is a case of "you and a donkey"!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his proof. The cucumber case is exactly like "you and a donkey", and the תרומה still takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fit outer part is like the "you", and the unfit bitter inside is like the "donkey". The ברייתא says the תרומה works, so the unfit part does not spoil the fit part. In the same way, the person acquires even though he was named together with a donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (here used to set up the proof)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's proof works like this. Fit and unfit parts of a cucumber are separated together as תרומה, and the תרומה takes effect. So an invalid partner does not cancel the gift to the valid receiver.

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: Why does the תרומה take effect, when part of what he separated is unfit?

phrases.english: It is "you and a donkey"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 4 to the dispute in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the valid receiver in "you and a donkey" is not cancelled out by the donkey.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The cucumber תרומה works even though it includes the unfit bitter inside.

steps.title: The cucumber case is different: the bitter part is real תרומה by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב ששת's proof, since by Torah law even the bitter part counts fully as תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because by Torah law it is proper תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's proof from the cucumber. It says that case is not really a mix of valid and invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת assumed the bitter inside was an invalid part joined to a valid part. The גמרא answers that by Torah law the bitter part is also good תרומה. So no invalid piece was ever included, and the case proves nothing about "you and a donkey."

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case doesn't compare
By Torah law (not just rabbinic law)

steps.confusionAlert: This doesn't mean it's fine to separate bitter produce as תרומה from the start. It only means that once someone does it, it works by Torah law.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" is רב ששת's cucumber case from steps 4 and 5.

phrases.english: for by Torah law
it is proper תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's proof from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from תרומה, not רב ששת's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the bitter part was invalid, but by Torah law it is valid תרומה, so there was no mix of valid and invalid.

steps.title: רבי אילעא's source: separating from bad for good still makes תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא proves from a פסוק that תרומה taken from poor produce for good produce still counts as תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אילעא said: How do we know that if someone separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, his תרומה counts? The פסוק says, "You shall bear no sin because of it, when you lift up its best part." If it weren't holy, why would there be any sin? So we learn that his תרומה counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim from step 6 with רבי אילעא's teaching. Bad produce given as תרומה still becomes real תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק implies that giving the poorer part is a sin. Something can only be a sin if it actually did something, so the poor produce must really become תרומה. That supports step 6: the bitter part is real תרומה by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce
Bearing sin; being guilty of a wrongdoing
Its best part (here, not literally fat)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ile'a said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרַע עַל הַיָּפֶה –
phrases.english: From where do we know, regarding one who separates from the bad for the good,
that his teruma is teruma?
For it is said: "And you shall bear no sin because of it,
when you set apart its best part from it"
And if it does not become holy,
why is there bearing of sin?

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרַע עַל הַיָּפֶה,
phrases.english: From here we learn, regarding one who separates from the bad for the good,
that his teruma is teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 6's claim that poor produce is real תרומה by Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: That תרומה from inferior produce is valid by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אילעא's reading of במדבר 18:32: "bearing sin" shows the act took effect.

steps.title: רב אויא brings the case of the five women
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא challenges רב המנונא with a משנה. A man tried to betroth five women together, two of them sisters, and the חכמים said the sisters are not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: רב אויא raises an objection. There was a case of five women, two of them sisters. A man picked a basket of figs that were theirs, from שביעית. He said, "You are all betrothed to me with this basket," and one of them accepted it for all of them. The חכמים said: the sisters are not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב המנונא, who said "you and a donkey" means nothing. It first quotes the case it will use. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man cannot be married to two sisters at the same time, so the two sisters cannot receive his קידושין together. That makes this a case of valid receivers (the other three women) grouped with invalid ones (the sisters). It looks a lot like "you and a donkey."

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi,
Rav Avya raises an objection:
phrases.notes: The objection is against רב המנונא from step 3, who said "you and a donkey" means nothing.

phrases.english: There was an incident with five women,
and among them were two sisters,
and one man gathered a basket of figs,
and it was theirs,
and it was of the Sabbatical Year;
and he said: "You are all hereby betrothed to me
with this basket";

phrases.aramaic: וְקִבְּלָה אַחַת מֵהֶן עַל יְדֵי כּוּלָּן.
phrases.english: and one of them accepted it on behalf of all of them.
The Sages said:
The sisters are not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה discussion and goes back to the three opinions in step 3, setting up a challenge to רב המנונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's view that "you and a donkey" means nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a case where valid and invalid receivers are grouped together in one act of קידושין.

steps.title: Why are the other women betrothed? It is "you and a donkey"!
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה we can infer that the non-sisters are betrothed. That goes against רב המנונא, since the case is like "you and a donkey."
steps.simpleTranslation: Only the sisters are not betrothed, which means the unrelated women are betrothed. But why? It is "you and a donkey"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the real question. The משנה implies the other three women are betrothed, so why doesn't the invalid part (the sisters) cancel everything, as רב המנונא would say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If including someone who can't receive ruins the whole statement, then including the sisters should have made the קידושין fail for everyone. But the משנה only rules out the sisters, so the other women are betrothed. This goes against רב המנונא, and fits better with the views that the valid receiver still gets something.

keyTerms.meaning: Unrelated women (here, the three who are not sisters)
"You and a donkey": a valid receiver joined with an invalid one

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source brought directly against רב המנונא. It shows the debate from step 3 also matters for קידושין, not only for gifts.

phrases.english: It is the sisters who are not betrothed,
which implies the unrelated women are betrothed;
but why?
It is "you and a donkey"!
phrases.notes: The sisters are like the donkey, someone who can't receive, joined to the women who can.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחָיוֹת הוּא דְּאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁוֹת הָא נָכְרִיּוֹת מְקוּדָּשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 8 and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that "you and a donkey" means nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the valid women are betrothed even though invalid women (the sisters) were included. So an invalid receiver does not cancel the whole statement.

steps.title: The sisters were never included in the betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the challenge from the five-women משנה. That משנה is talking about a man who only meant to betroth the women who are allowed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: That is why I saw רב הונא בר אויא in my dream. It was a sign that רב אויא would bring a challenge. But didn't we already explain that the משנה is talking about a man who said, 'Whoever of you is fit to be with me shall be betrothed to me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from steps 8-9. He shows that the משנה about the five women does not go against רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man only spoke to 'whoever of you is fit for me,' so the two sisters were never part of his words at all. That means nothing invalid was mixed into the deal. This is not like 'you and a donkey,' where a valid part and an invalid part are joined together.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why / this is exactly
We established it as talking about a certain case
The one who is fit to be with him (a woman he may marry)

steps.whatToRemember: The five-women משנה is no proof against רב המנונא. The man only included the women fit for him, so the sisters were left out from the start.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is why I saw
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי talking to רב מרדכי, the one bringing the challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Avya in a dream —
phrases.notes: The name אויא in the dream was a hint that רב אויא's challenge was coming.

phrases.english: because Rav Avya raises an objection.
Didn't we establish the משנה
as where he said: "Whoever of you is fit to be with me
shall be betrothed to me"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב המנונא raised in steps 8-9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה looked like a valid part and an invalid part joined together, where the valid part still works.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man only spoke about the women fit for him, so the sisters were never included and nothing invalid was mixed in.

steps.title: Property given to a wife and her sons
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a man gave his property 'to you and your sons.' רב יוסף rules that the wife gets half.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to his wife, 'My property is for you and for your sons.' רב יוסף said: She acquires half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic with a real case. רב יוסף gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man named his wife on one side and her sons as a group on the other, but he did not say how much each gets. רב יוסף reads it as two sides: half for her and half for all the sons together.

phrases.english: A certain man who said to his wife:
"My property is for you and for your sons,"
Rav Yosef said: She acquires half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the קידושין discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man gives his property 'to you and your sons,' the wife gets half.

steps.title: The proof from אהרן and his sons
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves his ruling from רבי's teaching that the לחם הפנים is half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Where do I learn this from? From a ברייתא. רבי says: 'And it shall be for אהרן and his sons' means half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to back up his ruling that the wife gets half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names one person (אהרן) and a group (his sons), and רבי splits it half and half. רב יוסף says our case has the same wording, one person and her sons, so it gets the same split.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: Rabbi says:
"And it shall be for Aaron and his sons" —
half for Aaron, half for his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רב יוסף's ruling in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a gift to 'one person and his group' is split half and half.

steps.title: אהרן is different from a wife
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. אהרן would get a share anyway, so naming him must mean half. A wife does not inherit, so it is enough that she gets one son's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It makes sense there. אהרן gets a share anyway, so the Torah named him separately to tell us he takes half. But a wife is not an heir, so it is enough for her to take the same as one of the sons.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. He shows that the case of אהרן is not like the case of the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן is a כהן who would have received a share even without being named. So naming him separately must teach something extra, which is half. A wife has no share in the property at all, so naming her only shows she is included, like one more son.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense in that case

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the wife gets nothing. He is saying she gets the same as one son, instead of half of everything.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Granted there,
Aaron is someone who gets a share;
that is why the Merciful One named him separately —
so that he takes half.
But a woman is not one who inherits,
phrases.notes: A wife does not inherit her husband's property, so she has no share to begin with.

phrases.english: it is enough for her to take like one of the sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 12 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from אהרן. It does not prove the opposite.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אהרן already had a share, so naming him adds 'half.' A wife has no share, so naming her only includes her as one of the sons.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן gave half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי with real cases. In נהרדעא שמואל collected half, and in טבריה רבי יוחנן collected half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But there was a case in נהרדעא, and שמואל collected half for the person! And in טבריה, רבי יוחנן collected half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's idea using real court cases where the single person was given half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great judges ruled in practice that when one person and a group are named, the one person gets half. That supports רב יוסף's reading and goes against אביי's 'like one of the sons.'

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But there was a case in Nehardea,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't spell out the case, but it means one like ours: a gift to one person and a group.

phrases.english: and Shmuel collected half for him!
In Tiberias, and Rabbi Yochanan collected half!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that the named person gets only one share like the others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל and רבי יוחנן both ruled in real cases that the single named person gets half.

steps.title: רבי split the crown tax half and half
steps.stepSummary: A further challenge: רבי ruled that a royal tax placed on two groups is paid half by each group.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said there was a crown tax that the royal house placed on the city councilmen and on the important citizens. רבי said: The councilmen should pay half and the important citizens should pay half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more case against אביי, this time from רבי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sides are named together, רבי split it evenly between them. He did not count heads. This again supports reading 'X and Y' as half and half, and it goes against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Crown money (a tax for the king)

steps.whyThisMatters: Three separate rulings, from שמואל, רבי יוחנן and רבי, all read 'one side and another side' as half and half. That puts heavy pressure on אביי's position.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר:
phrases.english: And furthermore, when Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:
A certain crown tax
that the royal house imposed
on the city councilmen and on the important citizens,
Rabbi said: Let the councilmen give half
and the important citizens half!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more case to the challenge of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that the named side gets only an equal per-person share.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי split a tax between two named groups evenly, half and half, without counting heads.

steps.title: The royal tax case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי's tax ruling. That half-and-half split came from the special history of the tax, not from the wording alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a fair comparison?! In that case, at first, when they wrote the tax order, they wrote it only on the city councilmen. The leading citizens used to help them pay, and the king knew they were helping. So now, when they wrote it on the councilmen and on the leading citizens, they meant that each group pays half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from Step 15. It says the royal tax case cannot be compared to a gift to 'you and your sons.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the tax was written only on the councilmen, and the leading citizens helped out on the side. When the king added the leading citizens by name, he was formally making them equal partners, so each group pays half. That split comes from the history of this tax, so it proves nothing about the wife in רב יוסף's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a fair comparison?! A phrase that rejects a comparison
Leading citizens, important people of the city

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the tax ruling is wrong. It agrees each group pays half. It is only saying this case cannot serve as a proof, because its background is different.

phrases.english: Is that a fair comparison?!
There, at first, when they would write the tax order,
they would write it on the city councilmen alone;
and the leading citizens would help them pay,
and the king knew that they were helping;
so now, the fact that they wrote it
on the councilmen and on the leading citizens
is to say that these pay half and those pay half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the tax-case challenge raised in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the royal tax. The other challenges (Step 14) are not addressed here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The half-and-half tax split came from the tax's history: the leading citizens were already helping and were now being made equal partners. It does not come from a general rule about wording.

steps.title: A מנחה promised in two vessels is not split in half
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רב יוסף from a ברייתא. A promise of one hundred עשרונים 'in two vessels' is brought as sixty and forty, not fifty and fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא raised a challenge: If someone says 'I take upon myself to bring a מנחה of one hundred עשרונים, to bring it in two vessels,' he brings sixty in one vessel and forty in the other vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רב יוסף's ruling that the wife gets half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that splitting something between two named parties means two equal halves. Here, the person said 'two vessels,' yet the split is sixty and forty, not fifty and fifty. So mentioning two parts does not automatically mean equal halves.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises a challenge from an earlier source
'I take upon myself,' the wording of a vow to bring a קרבן
A tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'two parts' can be unequal, which goes against the logic behind רב יוסף's half-and-half ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised a challenge:
One who says: 'It is upon me to bring a meal-offering of one hundred tenths,
to bring it in two vessels'
brings sixty in one vessel,
and forty in the other vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tax proof is pushed aside, a new challenge is aimed directly at רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling (Step 11) that the wife gets half when property is given 'to you and your sons.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Splitting something into two parts does not have to mean two equal halves. A מנחה promised 'in two vessels' is brought as sixty and forty.
